intro: Lesson 17: First aid basics: the primary survey and the recovery position. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.h: First aid guide (check against current NHS and Resuscitation Council UK guidance)

head: Situation
What to do
rows: Check for danger to you and others before helping.
Call 999 (speaker on) and start chest compressions: hands in the centre of the chest, push hard and fast; use a defibrillator (AED) as soon as one arrives and follow its instructions.
Put them in the recovery position and call 999; keep checking their breathing.
Press firmly on the wound with a clean pad and call 999.
Encourage coughing; then up to 5 back blows; then up to 5 abdominal thrusts; call 999 if it does not clear.
Cool under cool running water for 20 minutes; cover loosely with cling film; get help for serious burns.

blocks.note: TO CONFIRM: check this guide against a recognised first aid syllabus and the current NHS and Resuscitation Council UK guidance before use.

panels.title: If breathing: recovery position
points: Arm nearest you at a right angle
Back of the other hand to the cheek
Bend the far knee, roll towards you
Tilt the head to keep the airway open

panels.title: If not breathing
points: CPR: push hard and fast in the centre of the chest, about 100 to 120 a minute
Use a defibrillator if one is brought

keywords.def: the person who is hurt or ill
a safe position for someone unresponsive but breathing
chest compressions and rescue breaths for someone not breathing

questions.q: The first D in DRABC stands for ...
Think again: If someone collapsed in front of you, what would stop most people helping?
questions.a: Fear of doing it wrong; knowing simple steps gives confidence, and calling 999 is always right.
